newsitem.title: USA: Texas cotton condition continues to improve.
newsitem.headline: Texas cotton condition continues to improve.

text.p: Condition of the Texas cotton crop continued to improve during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
Cotton condition was rated 77 percent of normal, against 76 percent last week and 66 percent last year.

"Bolls continued to set in the Blacklands," the service said in its weekly crop progress report. "Bolls are starting to open in the South Central area and continued opening in the Coastal Bend and along the Upper Coast."
Eighty-nine percent of cotton was squaring, ahead of 80 last week, 89 last year and the average of 78 percent.
The report said the state's sorghum crop was in need of rain, but most fields looked good. Sorghum was rated 84 percent of normal, versus 83 percent last week.
Corn condition was rated at 87 percent of normal, ahead of 86 percent last week and 59 percent last year. Corn was 61 percent silked versus 93 percent a year ago and the average of 81 percent.
The Texas wheat crop was 99 percent harvested, against 95 last week, 99 last year and the average of 98 percent.
Range and pasture condition was rated 64 percent good to excellent, below 66 percent at that level last week.
